results.text:
**Verdict:** I resubmitted the deck as a **brew** (Tron shell, Karn and The One Ring as the core). It is only a small upgrade on the original, and I couldn't make the bigger changes I wanted. The submit step rejects any list that is more than 60% identical to a real Tron list, so I couldn't copy the stock build. My first three revisions (Ugin, Saga and Nexus to 4, Command to 4) were rejected at 71.7%, 66.7% and 63.3%.

**Plan:** Reach Tron or an Ancient Tomb or Grim Monolith start on turns 2–3. Cast The One Ring or Karn, the Great Creator ahead of schedule. Karn's −2 fetches sideboard artifacts to answer whatever you face (Tormod's Crypt, Lattice, Pithing Needle and so on). Close with Wurmcoil Engine, Cityscape Leveler, Emrakul, Walking Ballista, or the Mycosynth Lattice lock.

**What I changed:**
- **Planar Nexus 2 → 3, replacing one Urza's Cave.** Nexus counts as an Urza's Mine, Power-Plant and Tower at once, so it completes Tron with fewer lands. I looked up the card text. I didn't simulate this effect, because the simulator only models plain mana.
- **Ugin, Eye of the Storms was tried and cut.** It is in 94.4% of recent Tron lists, but it pushed the list over the similarity cap.
- **Meteor Golem is still in the main deck.** It is a weak slot that I could have swapped out if the cap had allowed.

**Mana:** 23 lands: 4 each of Tower, Mine, Power-Plant and Ancient Tomb, 3 Planar Nexus, 2 Urza's Saga, and 1 each of Inventors' Fair and Urza's Cave. Accelerants are 4 Expedition Map, 4 Grim Monolith, 2 Lotus Petal, Mind Stone and Everflowing Chalice.
- The simulator measured the earlier 23-land version at 66.9% for land drops through turn 4. The real Tron list measured 71.1%. That version had about 10% screw, 17.9% mulligans and 42.9% with the engine ready by turn 4.
- I did not re-simulate the final list. A variant with 4 Saga and 24 lands reached 70.3% land drops and 15.7% mulligans, but the cap kept me from submitting it.
- Colour is never a problem, because the deck is colourless.

**Matchups (judgment from the meta data):**
- **Dimir Tempo (13.2% of the field):** This is the worst matchup. Counterspells and Wasteland hit a 4-mana engine and the Tron lands. Mana rocks and Solemn help you recover. Bring in Dismember and Pithing Needle, and Trinisphere if you can cast it.
- **Ocelot Aggro (7.9%), Initiative (3.6%) and Death and Taxes (3.7%):** Ancient Tomb's damage hurts here. The One Ring's protection, Kozilek's Command and Wurmcoil help. Bring in Dismember, Ensnaring Bridge and Torpor Orb. Take Disruptor Flute out of this matchup.
- **Reanimator (7.1%), Doomsday (6.9%) and Sneak and Show (3.4%):** Fetch Tormod's Crypt with Karn. Bring in Disruptor Flute and Pithing Needle.
- **Blink (4.9%):** Torpor Orb and Engineered Explosives.
- **Mirrors and Affinity:** Bring in Cityscape Leveler and the second Mycosynth Lattice.
- **Sideboard:** Take out Meteor Golem, Battlesphere and slow cards in the fast matchups.

**Unverified:**
- I never tested win rates against any matchup.
- Candelabra of Tawnos shows up in Tron results, but the tool lists it as banned in Legacy, so I left it out.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Fanatic of Rhonas, Slumbering Trudge and Fight Rigging.
results.text:
**Plan.** Cast Slumbering Trudge for {G} on turn 1. It's a 6/6 that turns on ferocious even while tapped and stunned. That makes Fanatic of Rhonas tap for GGGG and doubles Whisperer of the Wilds and Ilysian Caryatid. Fight Rigging then makes Trudge a 7-power creature, so you get a free hideaway card each turn. The mana pays for Hulking Raptor, Elder Gargaroth and Craterhoof Behemoth.

**Changes from the submitted list.** I kept the engine and changed the shell and mana.
- **Nature's Rhythm ×2 out.** It needs a large X to find anything above Trudge, and Green Sun's Zenith already fetches Trudge for 2 mana.
- **Rhonas the Indomitable ×1 and Outcaster Trailblazer ×1 in.** These are my picks from a card search. Rhonas is a 5-power indestructible 3-drop that enables ferocious and is hard for Galvanic Discharge to kill. Trailblazer is a 4-power ferocious enabler that draws cards when other big creatures enter. Both are judgment calls, not measured.
- **Cavern of Souls out, one Forest in.** In a mono-green deck Cavern mostly makes colorless mana, and it can't help cast Fanatic, which is a Snake. The deck is now 19 Forest and Boseiju, Who Endures, for 20 lands, all producing G.

**Matchups.** These are judgment from the meta and archetype lists, not simulated games.
- **Energy (16.6% of the field).** This is the worst matchup. Its lists run Galvanic Discharge ×4, Phlage and Ragavan, and they board Wrath of the Skies. A dork-heavy start that hasn't landed Trudge is exposed. Trudge, Rhonas and Raptor (ward 2) are the best draws. Dismember and Tireless Tracker come in for the longer games.
- **Affinity (9.9%).** This is a close matchup. Its lists main Engineered Explosives and Tormod's Crypt and often board Whipflare and Damping Sphere. Bring in Force of Vigor ×2 and Collector Ouphe ×2, and keep Boseiju as a free answer.
- **Storm and Goryo's Vengeance.** The deck can't interact with these. Bring in Endurance ×2 against Goryo's Vengeance and Damping Sphere against Storm. Otherwise race them.
- **Blood Moon.** This isn't a problem for a mostly Forest mana base, because basics stay basics. Only Boseiju turns into a Mountain.
- **Control and Blink.** Keep Veil of Summer ×2 in against blue, black and red decks. Beast Within ×2 is mainly for problem permanents such as Urza's Saga or a Blood Moon you can't play through.

**Mana (simulated, 5,000 games).**
- The revised 20-land list has 8.4% mulligans and 100% color-OK every turn.
- Average lands in play are 1.86 on turn 2, 2.57 on turn 3 and 3.13 on turn 4.
- The screw rate in the earlier run of the original list was 25.6%. The revised list repeated that figure exactly (25.6%), so the land swap didn't change it. That's high for a deck that wants to curve out, but the 14 dorks cover some of it.
- The Trudge-plus-Fanatic pairing is in hand by turn 3 in 56.3% of games. It's also castable by turn 3 in 28.1%. That 28.1% counts only the cards in hand, not the ones Rumble or Zenith can fetch. The Devoted Druid Combo comparison gave 60.7% for the pairing in the earlier run. The 56.3% and 28.1% figures were measured on the revised list.
- Two other things in the engine are unmeasured. I haven't simulated Fight Rigging reaching 7 power or hitting a hideaway card. I also haven't simulated Craterhoof being cast.

**Label.** Brew. It borrows its mana-dork and Green Sun's Zenith structure from Devoted Druid Combo. Fight Rigging and Hulking Raptor have no recent tournament results (0 lists in 90 days), so those slots are untested.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Warren Soultrader, Gravecrawler and Marionette Apprentice.
results.text:
**Plan.** This is mono-black Zombie aristocrats. Warren Soultrader turns a Gravecrawler into a Treasure. That Treasure pays to recast Gravecrawler from the graveyard, because Soultrader is a Zombie. With Marionette Apprentice, Blood Artist or Zulaport Cutthroat in play, each cycle drains the opponent. If the combo is disrupted, the cheap recursive creatures attack instead.

**What I changed after reviewing the first submission.** I kept the locked engine (4 Soultrader, 4 Gravecrawler, 4 Apprentice, plus Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bloodghast).
- **Orcish Bowmasters:** I added 4 and cut the 3 Cryptbreaker. The Soultrader Combo lists I pulled average 3.7 Bowmasters, so this matches what they play. Its pings are my judgment for beating Prowess's X/1 creatures and Lava Dart. Soultrader is already a Zombie, so losing Cryptbreaker costs little Gravecrawler support.
- **Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER:** I added 1 as an extra sacrifice outlet and drain piece. About two-thirds of the proven lists play it.
- **Village Rites:** I cut it from 2 to 1 to make room.
- **Swamps:** I cut one Swamp, so 13 Swamps, 2 Spymaster's Vault, 1 Phyrexian Tower and 2 Bloodstained Mire, plus 2 Boggart Trawler as land-spells.
- **Sideboard:** The old board had 2 Culling Ritual and 2 Haywire Mite, and I removed both. Culling Ritual needs green mana this deck can't make. Haywire Mite's ability needs green too. I replaced them with 2 Inquisition of Kozilek and 2 Collective Brutality.

**Mana (simulation, 5,000 games).**
- **Colour:** Black was available on time in 100% of games through turn 6, because the deck is mono-black.
- **Mulligans:** The final list mulligans 9.0% of the time. The first submission mulliganed 8.4%, and a 17-land version mulliganed 9.6%.
- **Engine:** At least one engine piece was in hand by turn 4 in 90.8% of games, and castable in 87.6%. The first submission measured 88.3% castable, so the revision costs about 0.7 points here.
- **Land count:** The tool flagged 19 lands against about 21 in the proven lists. The simulator doesn't count Trawler as a land, so I can't confirm the exact real count. I judge the deck to be near the proven list's mana.

**Matchups.** The meta shares come from the tool. The matchup assessments are my judgment, not measured.
- **Broodscale Combo (14.9%):** This is the worst matchup. The list plays Soul-Guide Lantern and Haywire Mite, and it is likely faster than this deck. Be aggressive with Thoughtseize, and use Flare of Malice on a big Emrakul.
- **Prowess (10.7%):** Lava Dart and Lightning Bolt punish our 1/1s. Bowmasters and the recursive creatures help. Bring in Collective Brutality and Fatal Push.
- **Goryo's Vengeance (4.4%), Living End (2.3%) and other graveyard decks:** Bring in Dauthi Voidwalker, Surgical Extraction and Nihil Spellbomb. Dauthi also exiles our own opponent's cards, not ours.
- **Blink (6.7%), Affinity (5.5%) and Eldrazi Tron (4.8%):** Add Fatal Push for their cheap creatures. Inquisition of Kozilek is also a good draw against these decks.
- **Control (Jeskai, UW):** Trim Flare and Push, and bring in Inquisition of Kozilek.
- **Our own weakness:** Graveyard hate such as Soul-Guide Lantern, Scavenger Grounds and Rest in Peace is the deck's biggest risk. Cut Village Rites and Unearth for more interaction if you expect it.

**Label.** This is a brew that borrows its shell and mana from the Soultrader Combo archetype (15 lists). It drops that archetype's Chthonian Nightmare, Phoenix Fleet Airship and Malevolent Rumble, and it runs more cheap Zombies.

**Unverified.** I didn't test the combo's speed, how many turns it takes to kill, or any matchup win rates. The simulator only models land drops and colours, not card abilities.

results.text:
**Deck status:** I revised the submitted list once and it was accepted. It is a brew, borrowing its mana and sideboard shell from the one Dimir Control list in the results, plus Terror and Faeries sideboard norms. The 4 Murmuring Mystic, 4 Thorn of the Black Rose, 4 Counterspell and 4 Think Twice core did not change.

**Plan.** You cast Thorn on turn 4 behind open mana and become the monarch for an extra card each turn. Every instant you cast makes Murmuring Mystic produce a 1/1 flying Bird. The Birds guard the monarchy and carry the damage in the air. Counters and cheap removal buy time. Thorn's deathtouch and Mystic's 1/5 body hold the ground.

**Changes from the submitted list (judgment, not simulated):**
- **2 Disfigure became 2 Cast Down.** Cast Down is a 2-mana instant that kills any nonlegendary creature. Disfigure's -2/-2 misses the creatures these decks actually play, such as Tolarian Terror, Cryptic Serpent, Gurmag Angler and Ninja of the Deep Hours. Cast Down is also what most Wildfire, Faeries and Golgari Gardens lists run.
- **1 Deduce became 1 Lórien Revealed.** It islandcycles for {1} to fix mana early and draws three late. It is a sorcery, but casting it still triggers Mystic. Contaminated Aquifer is an Island Swamp, so it can also be fetched.
- **Sideboard:** I cut Annul from 3 to 2. Its targets (Sleep of the Dead, Sewer-veillance Cam, Cryoshatter) are narrow. I added 2 Suffocating Fumes and 1 Steel Sabotage.

**Matchups.** This is a read from the meta and archetype data, not a simulation of matches.
- **Faeries (8.2%) and Terror (12.8%):** these are the hardest. They run Counterspell, Dispel and flyers that can take the monarchy. Their creatures are mostly blue (Spellstutter Sprite, Ninja, Delver, Tolarian Terror), so Snuff Out and Go for the Throat are live. The top Faeries lists play Thorn too, so the monarchy can swing back and forth. Your Birds and Dispel are the answer.
- **Madness (16.4%), Tron (10.3%), Ponza (6.6%), Elves (4.8%):** the engine's thesis lists Madness, Tron, Ponza and Elves as favourable. Elves is the weakest of those four.
- **Mono-Red Rally (3.2%):** the engine's thesis lists it as a loss. Lists that take the monarch early are the main risk.

**Mana.** The deck runs 21 lands: 14 blue sources and 12 black. Simulation, 5,000 games, on the pre-revision 21-land list:
- The mulligan rate was 8.7%.
- 77.7% of games had a Mystic or Thorn in hand by turn 4.
- Only 34.1% had that 4-drop castable on turn 4, because 4-mana cards on turn 4 with two colours are demanding.
- Colour was available 83.6% of the time by turn 5.
- A trial with 20 lands plus 2 Lórien Revealed gave a worse screw rate (25.6% against 21.8%). The simulator does not count islandcycling, so that figure is conservative. I kept 21 lands and 1 Lórien.
- I did not re-simulate the final list. The only mana change from the simulated one is replacing a Deduce with Lórien.

**Sideboarding:**
- **Against Madness, Ponza, Rally and Wildfire:** bring in the 3 Blue Elemental Blast and 2 Hydroblast, plus the 2 Relic of Progenitus against Madness. Take out the Exclude, Essence Scatter and Dispel, which do little against burn.
- **Against Faeries and Terror:** add Hydroblast only if they show red. Take out the Go for the Throat and Cast Down that are weak against their blue creatures. Bring in Arms of Hadar and Suffocating Fumes for their small flyers.
- **Against Tron and Affinity:** bring in Annul and Steel Sabotage.
- **Against Elves:** bring in Arms of Hadar and Suffocating Fumes.
- **Against Spy Combo:** bring in Relic of Progenitus and Extract a Confession.

**Unverified:** I did not simulate matchups, and I did not measure Mystic and Thorn together on turn 4 or later. The lines about how each matchup plays out are judgment.

**Plan.** This is a mono-blue storm-mill deck. Sapphire Medallion and Helm of Awakening make your one-mana spells cost nothing and Brain Freeze cost almost nothing. Lotus Petal, Gush and Daze add spells to the storm count for free. You cast Traumatize to cut the opponent's library roughly in half, then finish with Vision Charm (mills 4) and a Brain Freeze with a big storm count. Each Brain Freeze copy mills 3.

**Changes from the submitted list (one revision).**
- I cut Ray of Erasure, one Daze and one Portent, and added 2 main-deck Hydroblast and 1 Island.
- Hydroblast is a one-mana instant, so it adds to the storm count when it has no red target. It is also real removal or a counterspell against Sligh, Goblins and GR Zoo.
- Sligh and Goblins together are 21.9% of the meta (12.8% and 9.1%). The original list had no main-deck answer to them.
- Sideboard: Annul goes from 2 to 3 copies, because it counters artifacts and enchantments and Stiflenought's sideboards run 2.9 on average.

**Mana (simulated, 5,000 games).**
- The deck now runs 18 lands: 16 Island and 2 Mishra's Factory.
- Blue mana was available on time in 98.2% of games on turn 1, rising to 99.5% by turn 4.
- Mulligan rate was 9.0%.
- The "screw" rate fell from 37.4% to 33.5% with the extra Island. That is still high, and it is a real weakness.
- The chance of having an engine piece castable by turn 4 fell from 22.2% to 17.4%, because I traded some free spells for stability. The simulator only counts mana and colors, so it can't say how often the full combo goes off.

**Matchups (judgment from the meta; I didn't simulate matches).**
- **Best:** Stasis, Standstill, Enchantress and other slow decks that don't pressure a library. Stiflenought (11%) is a fair fight because it has counterspells and Stifle.
- **Worst:** Sligh, Goblins and Elves (about 32% of the field together). The deck does little before turn 4–5, and the milling comes late.
- **Library size:** a 60-card library is large. Milling it takes Traumatize and several Brain Freeze copies, so a single stripped hand or a counterspell can stop the plan.

**Sideboarding.**
- **Versus Sligh, Goblins and GR Zoo:** bring in 2 Hydroblast, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 3 Chill, 2 Powder Keg and 3 Chain of Vapor. Take out the 3 Helm of Awakening, which makes their spells cheaper too, plus 3 Traumatize and some Portent or Daze. Play for blocking with Mishra's Factory and for tempo, not the long combo.
- **Versus Elves:** bring in Powder Keg and Chain of Vapor. The red cards are dead against them.
- **Versus Stiflenought, Stasis, Enchantress and Standstill:** bring in 3 Annul. The Hydroblast and Blue Elemental Blast stay in against blue decks that run red-hate of their own. Annul stops their artifacts and enchantments (including Dreadnought) and protects your own plan.

**Label: brew.** It borrows its cantrip and Gush mana base from Stiflenought. The cantrip package is Portent, Opt, Gush and Daze, the 16 Islands match their average, and the 2 Factories match their 2.1.

**Unverified.**
- Traumatize and Sapphire Medallion had no recent tournament results, so I'm going on card text only.
- I did not measure how fast the full kill comes together.
- I did not measure win rates against any matchup.

results.prompt: Mono red prison but in Premodern?
results.text:
I submitted the most recent top list of the Mono-Red Land Destruction archetype, unchanged, as a stock deck. It was a 5-0 Premodern League list from 2026-10-01. The results show no "Mono red prison" list, and the Rogue reference list isn't red prison at all. Land destruction was the closest real mono-red resource-denial deck, so I used it as the stand-in. It is not the Winter Orb / Smokestack / Static Orb style of prison. Premodern has no Trinisphere or Chalice of the Void, and Strip Mine, Mana Vault and Grim Monolith are banned.

**Plan:** Stone Rain, Pillage, Wasteland, Rishadan Port and Avalanche Riders (a creature that destroys a land when it enters) keep the opponent short on mana. Black Vise, Mogg Fanatic, Mishra's Factory and the burn spells then finish them while they stumble. The deck is built to hurt opponents who need a lot of mana or specific nonbasic lands.

**Key cards:**
- **Stone Rain (4), Pillage (3), Avalanche Riders (4):** these are the land-destruction core. Avalanche Riders appears in 100% of the archetype's lists, averaging 3.6 copies.
- **Wasteland (4) and Rishadan Port (4):** both are 100% adopted. They deny mana without using a spell slot.
- **Black Vise (3) and Cursed Scroll (1):** these punish the opponent's hand while they're stuck on lands.
- **Lightning Bolt, Incinerate, Firebolt, Earthquake, Grim Lavamancer and Mogg Fanatic:** these remove blockers and finish the game.

**Mana (26 lands, 14 of them red sources):** This matches the archetype's real average of 26.3 lands. `check_deck` found no issues. In the 5,000-game simulation:
- **Mulligans:** 12.8% of games.
- **Land drops:** I hit all four land drops through turn 4 in 77.3% of games.
- **Mana screw / flood:** 5.3% of games were screwed and 5.9% flooded.
- **Red available on turn 3:** 80.8% of games, which is the weakest point because Wasteland and Port make colorless mana.
- **Land destruction ready by turn 3:** the cards (Stone Rain, Pillage, Avalanche Riders) were castable in 32.9% of games and in hand in 59.5%.

The simulation only models land drops and colors, not what the cards do.

**Sideboard (stock):**
- **Overload (4), Red Elemental Blast (4), Pyroblast (2):** against blue decks such as Stiflenought, UB Psychatog and Standstill. RED BLAST and Pyroblast counter blue spells, and Overload is meant for their artifacts. I didn't look up Overload's text, so that last part is from memory and not checked.
- **Anarchy (2):** against Enchantress and Terrageddon's white permanents. The tool confirms it destroys all white permanents.
- **Aftershock (2):** a sideboard card I didn't look up. I'd bring it in against creature decks, but that is my guess about its role.
- **Tormod's Crypt (1):** graveyard hate against Replenish and Hermit Druid Combo.

Against Terrageddon and Enchantress, which together are about 24% of the field, I'd expect a hard time. I haven't measured that matchup.

If you want a real Stax build with Smokestack, Sphere of Resistance and Ankh of Mishra, it would be a brew with no tournament results behind it. Smokestack and Sphere only show up as sideboard or fringe cards in this archetype.

intent.goal: A functional mono red prison deck for Premodern, using the format's card pool to lock down opponents with taxing and resource-denial effects.

results.prompt: Most competitive non-power nine vintage deck?
results.text:
I picked **Dredge**, submitted as a **stock** list. It is the only established Vintage deck I found that plays none of the Power Nine.

**Why Dredge.** The other top decks I pulled all run Black Lotus and the Moxen. That covers Lurrus Control, Mono-White Initiative, Raker Shops, Oath, Sphere Shops and Eldrazi. In the archetype data, Power cards show up in only 2–3% of Dredge lists. The base is the most recent top-finishing Dredge list I could pull: 8th place at Vintage Challenge 32 (4-3), dated 2026-10-11. I changed nothing. That is a mid-table finish, so "proven" here means a real Challenge top-8 list, not a title.

**Caveat on "most competitive".** Dredge is only 3.9% of the recent field (26 of about 670 lists). Lurrus Control is 21.2% and Mono-White Initiative is 12.1%. I did not measure whether Dredge beats the Power-based decks. "Most competitive" here means the best-supported deck without Power, not the best deck overall.

**Plan.** Cycle cards with Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder. That fills the graveyard, and Ichorid, Narcomoeba, Prized Amalgam and Hollow One come back or cheat into play. Grief and the free counters (Force of Will, Force of Negation, Mental Misstep) protect the engine.

**Key cards.**
- **Bazaar of Baghdad and the dredgers:** Golgari Grave-Troll, Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Thug, Shambling Shell and Creeping Chill. Bazaar is the only land. In the archetype data, Grave-Troll, Ichorid, Stinkweed Imp and Bazaar are in 100% of lists, and Serum Powder is in 97.9%.
- **Grief:** it takes the opponent's best card, and it can be cast for free by exiling a black card from hand.
- **Chalice of the Void:** one copy (89.4% of lists play it) to blank cheap spells.

**Mana.** The deck has 4 lands, all Bazaar, and no colored sources. The archetype averages 4.57 lands, with a standard deviation of about 2. The simulator isn't useful for this deck. It reported a 60.2% mulligan rate and 98.4% "screw", and it gave identical figures for the real Dredge list. That is because it only counts lands and Dredge doesn't cast spells off lands. I'm not citing those numbers as real consistency. In practice you keep hands with Bazaar, or with a cycler such as Serum Powder or a free spell, and plenty of dredgers. `check_deck` passed the 60-card main with no errors.

**Sideboard (15):** 4 Force of Vigor, 4 Sickening Shoal, 3 Force of Negation, 3 Wasteland, 1 Strip Mine.
- **Against graveyard hate:** this is the deck's main weak spot. Bring in Force of Vigor and Force of Negation. Against Leyline of the Void, Rest in Peace and Containment Priest, Force of Vigor is the key card. It is free, and the Mono-White Initiative list I looked at sideboards those cards. Take out Chalice and the weaker creatures.
- **Against Lurrus Control and Paradoxical Outcome:** they are fast and carry free counters. Keep the Grief and counter suite. Sickening Shoal is free removal for their small creatures, and Wasteland and Strip Mine can be strong against Workshop and utility lands. This is judgment, not tested.
- **Against Workshop decks (Shops):** Chalice is already in the main. Wasteland and Strip Mine are probably better against their lands than against Bazaar-based Dredge, but I haven't measured this.
- **Against Oath and Tinker:** they are slow to interact with the graveyard. Keep the Forces and cut the narrower sideboard cards. This is judgment, not tested.

**Unverified.** I did not look up card text with `card_info`. The deck's list, the sideboard plan and the matchup advice come from the reference list and archetype data, plus my own judgment. I did not measure matchup win rates.

results.prompt: Mono black tron in Modern?
results.text:
**Mono-black Tron: revised list (brew, borrowing the Eldrazi Tron shell)**

**Plan.** Assemble Urza's Mine, Tower and Power Plant with the help of Expedition Map, World Map and Urza's Cave. Then land a 7-mana-or-more threat a turn or two early. Those threats are Wurmcoil Engine, Grave Titan, Ugin (both versions), Karn Liberated and Ulamog. Until Tron is up, Thoughtseize, Thought-Knot Seer, Fatal Push, Infernal Grasp, Dismember and Kozilek's Command buy time. Swamps make the black mana.

**What I changed from the submitted list (shell, mana and sideboard only; the engine is untouched):**
- **Ghost Quarter became an 8th Swamp.** The simulation compared the two builds.

| Measure (simulated, 5,000 games) | Original (7 Swamp + Ghost Quarter) | Revised (8 Swamp) |
|---|---|---|
| Black mana available on turn 4 | 82.9% | 86.5% |
| Tron lands in hand by turn 4 | 13.6% | 15.7% |

  Ghost Quarter moves to the sideboard for Urza's Saga decks.
- **Night's Whisper ×2 became Fatal Push ×2.** The top decks are fast, so cheap interaction beats card draw. Push kills 2-mana threats like Basking Broodscale. That is judgment, since I didn't check which cards Push hits.
- **I tried 21 lands and rejected it.** Screw rose to 22.7% (it was 11.5%), so I kept 22.
- **Sideboard:** Thoughtseize, Night's Whisper and Ghost Quarter are in; Fatal Push ×2 moved to the main deck.

**Mana (simulated).** The 22 lands are 4 Mine, 4 Tower, 4 Power Plant, 2 Cave and 8 Swamp. The final 60 weren't re-simulated. The test list had 61 cards, with a third Thoughtseize and no Ghost Quarter or Swamp swap difference beyond that.
- Mulligan rate is about 20%, and screw is about 11%.
- Flood is about 1.5%.
- Having all three Tron lands in hand by turn 4 is only about 16%. The deck relies on the Maps and Cave to find the rest, and the simulator doesn't model their abilities. So the real turn-4 Tron rate is higher than 16%, but I haven't measured it.
- Grave Titan's BB is the awkward cost with 8 Swamps. Fetching a Swamp with Map or Cave helps.

**Matchups.** Shares come from the meta data.
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%), Storm, Goryo's Vengeance and Living End** are the worst matchups. They are fast, and Tron can't interact until turn 3 or later. Thoughtseize, Thought-Knot Seer, Fatal Push and Kozilek's Command are the main-deck answers. Karn, the Great Creator is one of the few cards that comes in against Broodscale. Karn's static shuts off activated abilities of opposing artifacts. I didn't check whether that affects their combo pieces, so treat it as unverified.
- **Prowess (9.9%) and Affinity (5.4%)** are dangerous if Tron stumbles. Push, Grasp, Ballista and Wurmcoil help. Karn's static also stops Affinity's artifact abilities.
- **Eldrazi Tron (4.9%)** is a close mirror and a race to cast the bigger spells. Ugin and Karn Liberated exile its permanents.
- **Slower decks** (Rakdos Delirium, UW Control, Jeskai Control) are the best matchups, because Wurmcoil and Grave Titan outgrind them.
- **Boros Land Destruction** is fine only if Tron is already assembled.

**Sideboarding.**
- **Against Broodscale, Storm, Living End and Goryo's Vengeance:**
  - Bring in Grafdigger's Cage ×2 and Tormod's Crypt.
  - Bring in Relic of Progenitus, Pithing Needle and the third Thoughtseize.
  - Bring in Ghost Quarter against Urza's Saga.
  - Take out Wurmcoil Engine and the 7-drop Karn.
- **Against Affinity and Prowess:**
  - Bring in Toxic Deluge, Oblivion Stone and Ensnaring Bridge.
  - Take out Thought-Knot Seer.
  - Take out Ulamog.
- **Against Amulet Titan and Domain Zoo:** Damping Sphere and Chalice of the Void are options.
- **The sideboard is also Karn, the Great Creator's wish list.** Karn's −2 can fetch Chalice, Cage, Sphere, Needle, Relic, Crypt or Bridge from outside the game. I'm assuming your event allows wishing from the sideboard.

**Unverified.**
- Total win rates are not measured.
- Whether Karn's static stops Broodscale's combo pieces.
- How often Maps and Cave actually find Tron.
- Ulamog costs 10, so it is very slow.

results.text:
**Deck: City of Traitors mono-black aggro-discard (brew, borrowing the Moneyball Black shell).** I did not simulate this final 60. The mana figures below are from the closely related earlier version.

**Plan.** City of Traitors, Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal and Mox Diamond power out Phyrexian Negator, Hypnotic Specter, Priest of Gix and the shadow creatures on turns 1–2. Duress and Cabal Therapy clear the way. Edicts and cheap removal then protect the clock.

**Changes after reviewing the draft.**
- **Misses in the meta.** The draft's Terror and Royal Assassin showed 0 recent results in the tool, and Blackmail and Funeral Charm are weak. I cut all but one Terror.
- **Colorless lands and threats.**
  - Mishra's Factory is a colorless land that doubles as a threat. It appears in 21.7% of recent lists, and Moneyball Black plays 4.
  - The 14 Swamps and the 18 lands are now 12 Swamps, 4 City and 3 Factory.
  - Dauthi Slayer, Dauthi Horror and Black Knight add cheap black threats. Shadow dodges blockers and edicts.
  - Smother kills Sligh and Enchantress creatures, but Terror can't hit artifact creatures like Juggernaut.
- **Originality.** My first revision was rejected because 65% of it matched a real Moneyball list (the limit is 60%). The Dauthi and Black Knight package fixed that.

**Mana (measured on the earlier version, 19 lands plus Scrolls and Shades).**
- Mulligan rate was 8.6%.
- Screw rate was 29.8%, versus 34.1% for the original 18-land draft.
- The simulator counted at least one black source on 94.1% of turn-1 hands and 88.7% by turn 2. Colorless lands cost some color consistency.
- Only 17.5% of games had a threat and accelerant ready by turn 2. The simulator may undercount Dark Ritual.
- The deck check says 19 lands is light. It recommended about 20.8 lands, and real Moneyball lists run about 23.
- City of Traitors is sacrificed when you play another land, so it is weak late. That is a real cost of the deck.

**Matchups (from meta shares).**
- **Likely good:**
  - **Enchantress (12.5%):** discard plus Gloom from the sideboard.
  - **Hermit Druid and Replenish:** discard and graveyard hate.
  - **UB Psychatog:** discard and fast threats.
- **Likely bad:**
  - **Sligh (9.9%):** burn kills Specter and Negator, and Negator and Factory cost life. This is a judgment from card text, not a measured win rate.
  - **Terrageddon (11.2%):** the deck cannot recover from land destruction, and City is a liability against Wasteland.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** Vendetta, Snuff Out, Smother and Edicts all hit Juggernaut.

**Sideboard** (Engineered Plague 3, Dystopia 3, Gloom 2, Wasteland 2, Powder Keg 2, Withered Wretch 2, Tormod's Crypt 1). The Plague, Dystopia and Gloom plan comes from Moneyball Black's own sideboard.
- **Versus Enchantress:** bring in Gloom ×2 and Dystopia ×3, and cut Priest, Smother and Chainer's Edict.
- **Versus Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Engineered Plague (naming Goblin), Powder Keg and Withered Wretch. Cut Cabal Therapy, Duress and Black Knight.
- **Versus Terrageddon:** bring in Wasteland ×2, and cut the weakest removal. I am not certain Wasteland is good here, and you should watch your own land count.
- **Versus Hermit Druid and Replenish:** bring in Tormod's Crypt and Withered Wretch.

**Unverified.** I did not run matchup simulations, and none of this is a measured win rate.

results.text:
I submitted the most recent top-finishing 5 Color Psychatog list, unchanged, as a stock deck. I couldn't find anything called "Solution" in the card pool or the results data, so I assumed you meant the five-color deck. Tell me if "Solution" means something else.

**Plan:** The deck is a tempo-control build. It plays cheap threats (Meddling Mage, Quirion Dryad, Psychatog) and backs them with Counterspell, Daze, Swords to Plowshares and Fire/Ice. Gush, Opt, Portent and Sleight of Hand smooth the draws. Armageddon ends the game once you're ahead on board.

**Key cards:**
- **City of Brass, Gemstone Mine and Flooded Strand** (4 each) fix your colors.
- **Meddling Mage** is a cheap threat that taxes the opponent's key spell.
- **Armageddon** (2 copies) lets a small lead on board win the game.

**Mana:** The list has 19 lands plus Mox Diamond. The check tool counts these colored sources: W 14, U 19, B 9, R 9, G 9. The 5 Color Psychatog lists in the results average 19.2 lands, so this matches them.

In 5,000 simulated games:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 8.9% |
| Games short on lands (screw) | 28.7% |
| Games with too many lands (flood) | 0.2% |
| Colors castable on turn 3 | 85.3% |
| Colors castable on turn 6 | 90.4% |
| A creature or counterspell in hand and castable by turn 3 | 37.6% |
| A creature or counterspell in hand by turn 3 | 49.8% |

The check tool recommends about 21.6 lands, so the low land count is a trade-off. It leans on cheap spells: 29 of the 40 non-land cards cost 1 or 2 mana.

**Colors:** The main deck only uses white, blue, red and green, with black appearing only in the sideboard. It is a "five-color" deck only in the sense that the lands can produce all five colors. All cards fit within WUBRG.

**Sideboarding:**
- **Against red (Sligh, Goblins):** bring in Blue Elemental Blast and Pyroclasm. Blue Elemental Blast is the main answer to a red spell, and Pyroclasm clears small creatures.
- **Against Stiflenought and artifact decks:** bring in Seal of Cleansing and Ray of Revelation. Ray of Revelation also answers Enchantress, the most-played deck in the results (12.5% share).
- **Against black or creature decks:** bring in Engineered Plague and Duress.
- **Against slow or combo decks:** the sideboard has little for them. Armageddon is already in the main deck, so you can race them or hold counters.

**Unverified:** I didn't check how this list matches up against each deck in the field. The source list went 1-4 and finished 19th at Premodern Challenge 16, so it is proven to be playable, not shown to be the best. I made no changes to it.
